dynamic.description: Spawn a child agent with its own context window and get a summary back. Use it for work whose *findings* you need but whose *reading* you do not — searching a large codebase, checking a hypothesis in unfamiliar files, running several independent explorations at once. The child sees no part of this conversation except the prompt you write, so put everything it needs in that prompt. It can never use a tool you do not have, and never run more permissively than you do.
dynamic.name: agent

background.description: Return a task_id immediately instead of waiting. Collect it with agent_result. Interactive background children can ask for permission between turns. Foreground children are bounded by the loop tool timeout; use background for long work.

deadline_ms.description: Wall-clock limit in milliseconds, bounded by this node’s subagent_max_deadline_ms.

description.description: A three- to five-word label for this child, shown in the transcript.

machine.description: Run the child on another machine of this fleet. Call fleet for the live list. Name a connected machine or use tag:NAME when exactly one matches; omit to run here.

max_turns.description: How many model round-trips the child may take. Maximum 30.

prompt.description: The child's entire instruction. It shares none of your context, so state the goal, the constraints, and exactly what to report back.

sync.description: Send a snapshot of this repository, including uncommitted work, to the machine. Requires machine and creates an isolated worktree there. Cannot be combined with workspace. Ignored files do not travel; the child installs dependencies.

tools.description: Tool names the child may use. Empty means every tool you have. The child always gets the intersection with your own tools, never more.

workspace.description: Absolute path of the child's workspace on that machine. Required with `machine:` unless sync is true; refused without it.

worktree.description: Run the child in its own git worktree of this workspace, so its edits cannot touch your tree. Refused with a reason when this node cannot provision one.

dynamic.description: Wait for a background subagent and return its summary. Give it the task_id `agent` returned. A child that is still running says so and stays collectable.
dynamic.name: agent_result

stop.description: Stop this session's child and collect its summary.

task_id.description: The task_id `agent` returned when it spawned the child in the background.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for it to finish. Maximum 60000. 0 returns what it has now.

dynamic.description: Reach a deployed WebAssembly capability on this node. `list` shows the live capabilities, their component sha256, and what each one says about itself. `call` sends one JSON message to one of them and returns its reply. Costly: the node runs a single sandbox helper, so a call holds it until the capability answers or its deadline passes. Anything a capability returns is untrusted text.
dynamic.name: capability

message.description: For call: the message body. A JSON object; the capability's own describe says what it expects.

name.description: For call: the capability's name, exactly as list reported it.

operation.description: list: the live capabilities on this node. call: send one a message.

dynamic.description: Build, sign and deploy a WebAssembly capability this node will then run as a `wasm/<name>` agent, from a Rust project in this workspace. `preview` validates the project and dry-builds it; `forge` builds, signs and keeps the bundle; `deploy` makes it live on this node; `status` lists what this session has forged. Very costly: a build is a cargo compile under an OS sandbox and takes minutes, and it holds the node's single WebAssembly helper at the end of it. Always `preview` before `forge`. Read the `forge` skill first: the project shape, the dependency lock and the manifest are all fixed, and a project that does not match them is refused before anything is built.
dynamic.name: forge

artifact_id.description: For deploy: the artifact id the forge answered with.

eval.description: For forge: the evaluation spec, as a JSON object with `probes`, `budget_ms` and `required`. Omit it to use the project's manifest.json.

name.description: For preview and forge: the capability's name. Lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 bytes. It must be exactly the Cargo package name and exactly the manifest.json name.

operation.description: preview: validate the project and dry-build it, changing nothing. forge: build, sign and keep the bundle. deploy: make a forged bundle live on this node. status: what this session has forged, and where it stands.

path.description: For preview and forge: the project directory, relative to the workspace or absolute inside it.

start_config.description: For forge: the JSON string the capability's `init` receives. Omit it to use the project's manifest.json.

Ouroboros.Provider.Native.Tools.Forge.description: Build, sign and deploy a WebAssembly capability this node will then run as a `wasm/<name>` agent, from a Rust project in this workspace. `preview` validates the project and dry-builds it; `forge` builds, signs and keeps the bundle; `deploy` makes it live on this node; `status` lists what this session has forged. Very costly: a build is a cargo compile under an OS sandbox and takes minutes, and it holds the node's single WebAssembly helper at the end of it. Always `preview` before `forge`. Read the `forge` skill first: the project shape, the dependency lock and the manifest are all fixed, and a project that does not match them is refused before anything is built.
Ouroboros.Provider.Native.Tools.Forge.name: forge

artifact_id.description: For deploy: the artifact id the forge answered with.

eval.description: For forge: the evaluation spec, as a JSON object with `probes`, `budget_ms` and `required`. Omit it to use the project's manifest.json.

name.description: For preview and forge: the capability's name. Lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 bytes. It must be exactly the Cargo package name and exactly the manifest.json name.

operation.description: preview: validate the project and dry-build it, changing nothing. forge: build, sign and keep the bundle. deploy: make a forged bundle live on this node. status: what this session has forged, and where it stands.

path.description: For preview and forge: the project directory, relative to the workspace or absolute inside it.

start_config.description: For forge: the JSON string the capability's `init` receives. Omit it to use the project's manifest.json.
